notes.account: The opening reads “Notons les implications”. Display (5) contains two lines under a left brace, with a rightward double arrow on the upper line and a two-headed double arrow on the lower. The words “Si les” are live in this reading. Older capital and comparison strokes are retained. This is an account of the written statements, without a proof check.

“Nous poserons” introduces the equality chain labelled (6), beginning with a Sigma bearing a round sign and epsilon. The chain contains set-difference strokes, an intersection, and a primed epsilon. The right parenthesis has a dense omega/w glyph followed by an unresolved relation; the joined-left shape makes membership the first local reading.

Display (7) follows “de sorte que l’on a la décomposition”. It places E between two Sigma expressions with cup signs. The following prose says “de X en”, cancels the readable “trois”, and continues “ens. mutuellement disjoints.” The right parenthesis visibly contains a detached prime above each epsilon. Low earlier suffixes remain partly inseparable from revisions.

“Notons” introduces (8). Three long bars span a Sigma and its raised marks; the last Sigma has a detached dot above it and a comma between its round sign and epsilon. A separate low terminal mark remains uncertain. No interpretation of that mark is used to complete the formula.

The author cancels two abandoned prose openings: “On a le cas” and “on s’intéresse à la cond”. The latter stops after the d exit, with no observed i or abbreviation point. No authorial question, date, or explicit proof-check remark is visible in these lines.

The section heading is “1.2. Deux décompositions binaires”. Display (9) writes two indexed families. The following definition includes an underlined word read parallèles/paralèles, with non outside the underline. The whole interlinear phrase “si elles sont distinctes, et” is inserted before “s’il existe”; the long insertion rule turns downward at that attachment. H explicitly recognizes the whole interlinear addition, so macro-boundary differences are not reported as findings.

The lower sequence contains the disjointness display (10), then two inclusion displays with opposite exchanged indices/signs, labelled (11) and an uncertain 11-bis-like label. The connecting prose endings consist of two-stroke à/colon-like marks. The final display gives the two signed pairs. Its written second label digit remains 17/12-uncertain; numbering sequence was not used to replace the visible glyph.

Mathematical cues used during reading were strictly local: the repeated epsilons and detached primes, the shapes of 1 and 2 on adjacent Sigma terms, the omega form in the cleaner parenthesis, and the repeatedly written family symbol. These cues prompted attention to the strokes; they did not establish any theorem or license a corrected formula. In particular, the two primed epsilons in (7) and the open relation in (6) are retained.

There is no full-page title or date. The internal heading is 1.2. Deux décompositions binaires. A pencil 32 at the bottom left is retained as archive numbering in a TeX comment, not as an author page command. No drawing or diagram is present on this sheet.

No targeted proof check, independent re-proof, formal computation, or reuse-and-recheck of a mathematical result was performed. The check_events array is empty. Reading the displayed statements and comparing their written symbols has not been represented as mathematical verification.
